headline: Remote Wilderness Backcountry Orientation
reservation: While there are no entry permits for the park itself, all visitors should participate in a voluntary backcountry orientation at a visitor center. Commercial air taxis and private lodges require independent bookings months in advance. Always check with the National Park Service for the latest regarding bear-resistant containers and flight accessibility.

days.title: Arctic Foothills Flight

stops.name: Bettles Lodge
stops.detail: Finalize gear and coordinate with bush pilots at this historic aviation hub before departing for the park.

stops.name: Walker Lake
stops.detail: Explore the shores of this large alpine lake, a designated National Natural Landmark surrounded by spruce forests.

days.driving: Walking or local bush plane transfer only; no road access to park
days.note: Flight schedules are entirely weather-dependent; allow for significant delays in the Arctic.

days.title: Granite Spires and Tundra

stops.name: Arrigetch Peaks
stops.detail: View the dramatic, jagged granite spires that rise sharply above the Alatna River valley.

stops.name: Alatna River
stops.detail: Float or hike along this Wild and Scenic River to observe the diverse Brooks Range landscape.

days.driving: Cross-country walking or paddling; conditions vary by terrain
days.note: Expect slow travel across muskeg and tussocks; five miles is a full day for many hikers.

days.title: Nunamiut Culture

stops.name: Simon Paneak Memorial Museum
stops.detail: Learn about the Inland Iñupiat culture and their deep connection to the caribou herds.

stops.name: Anaktuvuk River Valley
stops.detail: Walk the surroundings of this remote village to experience the scale of the Brooks Range.

days.driving: Local walking; accessible only by scheduled air service from Fairbanks
days.note: Anaktuvuk Pass is a private community; stay on public land and respect resident privacy.

intel.title: Air Hub Staging
intel.text: There is no parking within the park; long-term staging occurs at air taxi bases in Fairbanks or Bettles. Confirm storage policies with your flight operator before arriving.

intel.title: Total Disconnection
intel.text: Cellular service is not available in the park interior. Carry a satellite communicator, offline GPS navigation, physical topographic maps and a compass, and know how to use them.

intel.title: Camp Stove Supplies
intel.text: Liquid fuel and canisters must be purchased in Fairbanks or gateway hubs before boarding bush planes. Air taxis have strict regulations regarding the transport of hazardous materials.

intel.title: Midnight Sun Window
intel.text: Mid-summer offers 24-hour daylight, allowing for flexible travel hours. By late August, the return of darkness increases the chance of seeing the aurora borealis.

intel.title: Roadless Wilderness
intel.text: Gates of the Arctic has no roads or maintained trails. Access is strictly by air taxi or strenuous cross-country hiking from the Dalton Highway corridor.

plan.arrival: Arrival in Fairbanks for final supply acquisition followed by a scheduled flight to Bettles for park orientation and bush plane departure.
plan.vehicle: No vehicles allowed in the park; 4WD is required only for those staging from the Dalton Highway via Coldfoot.
plan.goldenHour: The Arrigetch Peaks provide a dramatic silhouette during the extended arctic summer sunset.
